brief: Nvidia rebounded 31% and the SOX 14% on Jensen Huang's return as CEO, easing the leadership-vacuum risk that had Taiwan activate its stabilization fund and curb short selling, with South Korea preparing similar support. Investors feared a successor would rethink Nvidia's roadmap, supplier orders and AI financing. That fear has eased, but the note argues the Trump administration, Wall Street and Silicon Valley interests prevailing this round does not restore Asia's old normal. Huang's return adds a new board national-security export-control committee and a chief compliance officer, plus challenges to his open-weight-AI and China stance. New US remote-access chip rules mainly hitting Southeast Asia show restrictions have not peaked: Huang testifies before the Senate Banking Committee on 3 December and the House privately on 1 December, the backlash is bipartisan, and Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027. Pending measures include a DUV lithography export ban and a chip location-reporting requirement. For Asia, the resolved leadership risk eases export-demand and sentiment pressure, but the deeper US-China rivalry, where security outranks commerce, persists regardless of any Trump-Xi agreement.
